nodes_update.note: Hariwansh Lal Poonja; born between 1910 and 1913 (Wikipedia gives 13 October 1910 'or later'), so no year is used for the node; died 1997.
Prashant Tripathi; born in Agra; PrashantAdvait Foundation 2015; Vedanta online, mostly in Hindi. Birth year rests only on a COI-flagged Wikipedia article and is left out.

Shri Hit Premanand Govind Sharan Ji Maharaj; born Aniruddh Kumar Pandey, Akhri village, Sarsaul block, Kanpur district, UP. Birth year 1969 (NavbharatLive), 30 Mar 1971 (Wikipedia, citing ABP Live 2023) or 1972 (Pioneer column, citing a book by Anand Mishra and Resham Mukherjee); no year is used for the node. Left home at 13; naishthik brahmachari (Anandswaroop Brahmachari), sannyasa as Swami Anandashram; Varanasi ghats; Vrindavan (about two decades before 2025 per ThePrint); Shri Hit Radha Keli Kunj, Varaha Ghat. Living.
Born August 1888 (siddharameshwar.org, Wikipedia; one source gives 1875); initiated 1906 by Bhausaheb Maharaj; died 9 November 1936.

American co-founder and president of the Theosophical Society; arrived in Ceylon with Blavatsky May 1880; Dharmapala heard his first lecture there and later served as his translator; director of the Maha Bodhi Society from 1891; later broke with Dharmapala; founded free schools for outcaste children in Madras from June 1894 (BPS Wheel 281). Not subcontinent-born; tree node only. Dates 1832-1907 (born 2 Aug 1832, died 17 Feb 1907) confirmed by checker from standard references.
Occultist of the Cosmic Movement; the Mother met him in Paris in 1905 and worked with him and his wife Mary Ware at Tlemcen, Algeria, in 1906 and 1907 (Roshen Dalal; Mother's Agenda).

edges_upsert.note: Member from early 1884; went to Adyar December 1884; later broke with Olcott and the Theosophists over priorities and Theosophical universalism.

Heard Olcott in Colombo 1880; his translator on lecture tours from 1886; toured Japan with him 1889; Olcott director of the Maha Bodhi Society 1891; the two later broke, Theosophy Wiki citing differing priorities (Bodh Gaya vs general teaching) and McMahan citing Dharmapala's rejection of Theosophical universalism.

She met Théon in Paris in 1905 and stayed with him and his wife at Tlemcen in July to October 1906 and July 1907 (Roshen Dalal's biography of Sri Aurobindo; Mother's Agenda refers to her 'second time' there). Type influenced: no source read describes a formal initiation.
